findings.summary: The two codes' null marks coincide to within 2-3 px and the orange imas-efit set, drawn second and larger, hides the blue nova set: at the magnetic axis the rendered PNG carries 265 orange pixels against 6 blue, and at the admitted saddle 289 orange against 0 blue. The caption states both sets are drawn in their own code's colour, but a reader sees one. The underlying data do agree (the caption puts the nulls 0.017 m apart), so the figure does not mislead; the claim is simply not visible. Drawing nova's set as a hollow marker, or offsetting and annotating the coincidence, would make it visible.

ORANGE = '#c06a1b' is a burnt-orange/ochre hue of the family the project's figure style reserves for agentic marks and bans for ordinary data (the rule names #c65a12/#cc785c/#d97757 and the brown/olive family). imas-efit is a reference code, a physical comparison subject rather than agentic work, so it should take a clean hue. The hue is also legible at 3.9:1, so this is a style correction, not a readability defect.

No contour level value appears on any of the three panels: each draws twelve unlabelled contours, and only the combined panel's caption gives the generating span (-67.76 to -3.33 Wb of a 76.70 Wb span). A reader of either single-code panel cannot attach a flux to a contour, though the project rule asks for contours 'on stated levels'.

The two single-code panels each carry an in-figure title ('nova, white slice 0' / 'imas-efit, white slice 0') and a one-entry legend naming the same code again ('nova, reconstructed slice' / 'imas-efit, same slice'). The project style puts panel identity in the caption and needs no in-figure title, so the single-code panels spend ink on information the caption already carries.
